title: Cancellation for Nonpayment — HomeGuard Homeowners Policy Conditions
content:
**Condition 1 — Notice of cancellation for nonpayment.** Larkspur Mutual issues a notice of cancellation for nonpayment on a HomeGuard Homeowners Policy only when an installment has remained unpaid past the nonpayment notice period that starts on the installment due date. The nonpayment notice period is the package's nonpayment notice period in days, counted in calendar days from the due date recorded on the installment, so the notice may be issued from the day after the due date plus that number of days, and not on that day itself.

**Condition 2 — Scheduled cancellation date.** The scheduled cancellation date is the notice date plus the package's nonpayment cancellation notice period in calendar days. When a mortgagee is on file, the scheduled cancellation date is never earlier than the notice date plus the package's mortgagee notice period, and the notice is copied to the mortgagee.

**Condition 3 — Rescission.** The notice is rescinded only when the payments received after the notice date and before the scheduled cancellation date total at least the amount due as of the notice date. A partial payment does not rescind the notice.

The amount due as of the notice date is: the premium installments billed whose due date is on or before the notice date, together with fees assessed, returned payments, additional premium and refunds issued posted on or before it, less payments received, fees waived and return premium posted on or before it; never below 0.00. Payments and their dates are taken from the billing records of the policy under notice.

**Condition 4 — Cancellation.** When the scheduled cancellation date arrives without that cure, the policy is cancelled effective that date for nonpayment, and the unearned premium is credited pro rata, with no short-rate retention and no minimum earned premium.

**Condition 5 — Payment on or after the cancellation date.** A payment received on or after the cancellation date does not rescind anything. It is applied to the balance and can only support a reinstatement under the HomeGuard reinstatement terms.

## Timeline illustration (hypothetical)

Installment due 1 March; hypothetical nonpayment notice period 15 days; hypothetical cancellation notice period 10 days.

| Date | Position |
|---|---|
| 16 March (due date plus 15 days) | too early: no notice may be issued |
| 17 March | a notice may be issued if the installment is still unpaid |
| Notice issued 17 March | scheduled cancellation date 27 March |
| Payments received 18 to 26 March | count toward the cure |
| Payment received 27 March or later | does not rescind; applied to the balance |

With a mortgagee on file and a hypothetical mortgagee notice period of 12 days, the same notice of 17 March schedules cancellation for 29 March, because 27 March would be earlier than the notice date plus 12 days.

## Cure test (hypothetical)

Amount due as of the notice date: 412.00.

| Payments received after the notice date and before the scheduled date | Result |
|---|---|
| 412.00 in one payment | notice rescinded |
| 200.00 and 212.00 in two payments | notice rescinded (together at least 412.00) |
| 300.00 | not rescinded: partial payment |
